title: Vollmond (Full Moon)
note: A huge rock, a river across the stage, and rain that never stops. In Vollmond, Bausch's dancers hurl themselves through water until joy and exhaustion look the same. It's one of her most elemental, exuberant late works.

title: The Clown Master
note: A BBC Newsnight visit to the famously ruthless French clown teacher. Gaulier's school has trained actors such as Sacha Baron Cohen and Emma Thompson. His method is simple and brutal: find your pleasure on stage, or be told, very charmingly, that you are terrible.

title: Skid
note: The whole stage is tilted into a steep slope, and the dancers slide, tumble and cling to it. Gravity becomes Jalet's co-choreographer, turning falling into a kind of flight.

title: Cooped (highlights)
note: Spymonkey's breakout show is a spoof of overheated Gothic romance, performed by four clowns who commit to every terrible idea with total sincerity. It's a masterclass in the joy of failing gloriously.

title: Einstein on the Beach: Knee Play 5
note: The final interlude of the opera that rewrote what opera could be. Over Glass's hypnotic keyboard and chorus, a gentle spoken story of two lovers on a park bench closes almost five hours of trance-like theatre.

title: Le Salon (trio)
note: The Belgian company founded by Gabriela Carrizo and Franck Chartier makes dance that feels like a dream about to become a nightmare. Bodies bend in ways that seem impossible, inside rooms that look almost normal.

title: Radio Macbeth
note: Actors gather in an abandoned theatre to rehearse Macbeth as a radio play, and the tragedy seeps out of the microphones into their bodies. It's a great way into SITI's precise, ensemble-driven style.

title: The Statement
artist: Crystal Pite (performed by The Royal Ballet)
note: Four people around a conference table argue over who will take the blame. The dancers move to a recorded script by Jonathon Young, turning corporate double-speak into convulsive, astonishing movement.

title: Political Mother
note: Live drummers and a thundering rock band loom above the dancers, who surge and cower like a crowd under a dictator. Shechter composed the score himself. The result is part rave, part protest, and all adrenaline.

title: Dolmen Music
note: Six voices, a cello and percussion make sounds that feel older than language: keening, chanting, calling. Monk treats the voice as a whole body. Listen with headphones and let it work on you.

title: The Encounter
note: One man on stage, and every audience member wearing headphones. Using binaural sound, McBurney transports you into the Amazon with a photographer who got lost there in 1969. It's theatre that happens inside your head.

title: DESH
note: A solo about Bangladesh, his father, and the space between two homelands. Khan fuses kathak and contemporary dance inside breathtaking animated worlds designed by Tim Yip.

title: Kontakthof
note: Men and women in their best clothes line up in a dance hall to show off, flirt, wound and console each other. Bausch later restaged it with teenagers and with performers over 65. Here it's danced by the Paris Opera Ballet.

title: Sutra
artist: Sidi Larbi Cherkaoui, Antony Gormley & Shaolin monks
note: Real Shaolin monks, a boy, and a set of wooden boxes by sculptor Antony Gormley. The boxes become coffins, dominoes, a city and a lotus flower. It's a meeting of martial art and dance that still feels miraculous.

title: The Complete Deaths
note: Every on-stage death in Shakespeare, all 75 of them, performed by four clowns in one evening. It's absurd, inventive, and surprisingly moving about mortality.

title: Bedroom Folk
artist: Sharon Eyal & Gai Behar (Nederlands Dans Theater)
note: Dancers on high half-toe pulse as one organism to a relentless techno beat by Ori Lichtik. It's hypnotic, sensual and slightly sinister, like a club night run by a cult.

title: The Great Tamer
note: On a floor of loose boards, bodies appear, vanish and reassemble into living versions of Renaissance paintings. Papaioannou, a painter turned director, creates images you won't forget.

title: What the Body Does Not Remember
note: Vandekeybus's explosive debut: dancers hurl bricks at each other and dive at the floor, trusting instinct over thought. Nearly 40 years on it still feels dangerous.

title: Raoul
note: Charlie Chaplin's grandson alone on stage with a collapsing home and a few strange giant creatures. Clown, acrobatics, magic and loneliness all blur together in this solo.

title: Echad Mi Yodea
note: Dancers in a semicircle of chairs chant a Passover song while violently throwing themselves backwards, again and again. One dancer always falls. It's one of the most electrifying pieces of choreography ever made.

title: Les Médusées
note: Made for the Louvre at night, this piece has dancers seem to emerge from the museum's statues, petrified and then brought back to life, as if Medusa had passed through the galleries.

title: Old Hats
note: Two of America's great clowns, with bowler hats, bad luck and almost no words. Old Hats proves that a perfectly timed fall can still bring a theatre to its knees.

title: Akhnaten
note: Glass's opera about the pharaoh who tried to replace Egypt's gods with the sun. Phelim McDermott's production, starring countertenor Anthony Roth Costanzo, fills the stage with jugglers who keep time with the music.

title: Antigone
note: SITI strips Sophocles to its essentials: a few actors, a bare stage, and the timeless clash between conscience and the state. The tight, sculptural staging shows the Viewpoints approach at work.

title: The Rite of Spring
note: The stage is covered in earth, and by the end the dancers are covered in it too. Bausch's version of Stravinsky's ballet ends with a young woman in a red dress dancing herself to death. Few pieces of dance are this raw.

title: Betroffenheit
artist: Crystal Pite & Jonathon Young (Kidd Pivot / Electric Company Theatre)
note: Born from Jonathon Young's real-life tragedy, this piece looks at trauma as a room you can't leave, haunted by vaudeville routines and twitching bodies. It's devastating and brilliant theatre-dance.

title: Vessel
note: Dancers with their heads hidden become strange, headless sculptures around a white island in a pool of water. Jalet and the sculptor Kohei Nawa blur the line between body, object and myth.

title: Philippe Gaulier: The Man Who Waits for Freedom
note: A full-length documentary about the great clown teacher and the hopeful, terrified students at his school. Watch it in pieces if you like; it rewards the time.

title: Pruit Igoe (from Koyaanisqatsi)
note: In the wordless film Koyaanisqatsi, Glass's music swells over footage of a vast American housing project being demolished. It's one of the great marriages of image and sound.

title: Le Sous Sol (trio)
note: The third part of Peeping Tom's early trilogy goes underground, into a strange, half-remembered world. Watch for the bodies that seem to have no bones at all.

title: Café Müller
note: A dim café crowded with chairs, and dancers who move as if sleepwalking through grief and longing. Someone has to clear the path before they crash. Bausch's 1978 masterpiece still lands with startling force, and this teaser for the Paris revival shows why it is endlessly restaged.

title: Nelken (Carnations)
artist: Pina Bausch / Tanztheater Wuppertal & Terrain Boris Charmatz
note: A field of pink carnations covers the whole stage, and the dancers trample, tiptoe and play through it. Nelken is one of Bausch's most joyful and unsettling pieces, where sweetness and menace sit side by side. Here it returns, newly performed under Boris Charmatz.

title: Omphalos
note: Jalet's piece for Ceprodac, Mexico's national contemporary dance company. Omphalos means 'navel' in Greek, the ancient name for the centre of the world, and Jalet builds sculptural human images that feel both ancient and futuristic: a ritual about where we stand in the universe.

title: Babel (words)
artist: Sidi Larbi Cherkaoui & Damien Jalet, with Antony Gormley
note: Antony Gormley's huge metal frames become rooms, borders and towers that the dancers keep rebuilding. Starting from the Tower of Babel, Cherkaoui and Jalet stage a wild, funny and tender argument about language, territory and belonging.

title: The Kingdom of Humor and Fun
note: A short, beautifully shot documentary about Philippe Gaulier's clown school, featuring the master himself and his students. It captures the strange alchemy of his teaching: cruelty, tenderness and the relentless hunt for pleasure on stage.

title: Mad Rush
note: Philip Glass alone at the piano, playing one of his best-loved solo works. Mad Rush rocks between calm, rippling patterns and sudden storms of sound. Watching the composer play it himself makes it feel intimate, almost like overhearing a private thought.

title: Satyagraha
artist: Philip Glass / Phelim McDermott / English National Opera
note: Glass's hypnotic opera about Gandhi's years in South Africa, in Phelim McDermott's spectacularly theatrical staging. Giant puppets and simple materials conjure whole worlds, while the music builds a slow, overwhelming sense of peace as a force.

title: bobrauschenbergamerica
note: Charles Mee's collage play becomes a theatrical Rauschenberg combine: odd objects, American songs, picnics and sudden dances piled into one exuberant whole. SITI's ensemble moves with their trademark precision, finding poetry in the ordinary and the absurd.

title: Moby Dick (the falling-over routine)
note: Stephan Kreiss falls over. And over. And over again. Spymonkey's legendary routine from their Moby Dick turns a single pratfall into a masterclass in escalation, timing and the sheer stupidity of a body betrayed by gravity.

title: The Tempest Replica
note: Pite replays Shakespeare's storm and revenge story with masked, white-clad figures who move like puppets of memory, then retells it in raw, full-bodied dance. It's a ghostly, gripping piece about control and forgiveness.

title: Clowns
note: Made for BBC television, Shechter's film is a macabre comedy of murder and desire, set to his own pounding music. Dancers kill each other with gleeful flourishes and keep on partying. It is darkly funny and asks how far we'll go in the name of entertainment.

title: Triptych: The missing door, The lost room and The hidden floor
note: Characters trapped on a ship drift through rooms they can't escape, while bodies twist in impossible, unnerving ways. Peeping Tom builds cinematic dream-labyrinths where the floor is never quite solid, and this trailer drips with their dark, uncanny beauty.

title: Mary Said What She Said
note: Isabelle Huppert alone as Mary Stuart on the eve of her execution, carved out of Robert Wilson's sculpted light. A torrential monologue meets Wilson's frozen, painterly images, and the result is mesmerising.

title: Choosing Companions (from ATLAS)
note: A scene from Monk's opera ATLAS, in which an explorer gathers her travelling companions. Monk's wordless vocal music turns each character into a sound, a gesture, a whole personality. Strange, warm and completely her own.

title: Vertical Road
note: Inspired by Sufi tradition and the poet Rumi, Khan's ensemble travels from gravity to grace to Nitin Sawhney's score. Bodies whip, spiral and collapse with astonishing speed, then fall into stillness. It's ritual and physical thrill at once.

title: OCD Love
note: Inspired by Neil Hilborn's poem about love and obsessive-compulsive disorder, this piece is all tics, repetitions and missed connections. The dancers pulse on half-toe to Ori Lichtik's relentless techno, sensual and aching at the same time.

title: Transverse Orientation
note: Papaioannou weaves myth, religion and visual art into images that look like living paintings. His stage magic is handmade and astonishing: bodies are assembled, split and transformed before your eyes, with dry wit and real awe.

title: Au Revoir Parapluie
note: Acrobat, clown, musician and magician, James Thiérrée builds worlds where furniture rebels and bodies defy physics. This trailer captures his breathless mix of slapstick, poetry and circus. The grandson of Charlie Chaplin, he clearly inherited the gift for turning disaster into wonder.

title: Sadeh21
note: Batsheva's dancers move with Naharin's Gaga-fed mix of explosive power and strange softness. Sadeh21 builds field by field, from fragmented solos to a startling finale, and shows a company at the height of its physical intelligence.

title: The Regard of Flight
note: Bill Irwin, the great American clown, sends up the pretensions of avant-garde 'New Theater' while a critic heckles from the audience. Every hat trick, rubber-legged fall and fake manifesto lands with eccentric precision. A brilliant, very funny portrait of a performer at war with his own art form.

title: Out of Context – for Pina
artist: Alain Platel / les ballets C de la B
note: Dedicated to Pina Bausch, Platel's piece explores hysteria and madness through twitching, convulsing, stripped-back bodies. What starts as discomfort grows into something tender and strangely joyous, a tribute in her own spirit of radical honesty.

title: The Show Must Go On
note: A DJ plays pop hits, and the performers do exactly what the lyrics tell them, no more and no less. Bel's deadpan conceptual masterpiece is hilarious and unexpectedly moving, turning a stage of ordinary people into a mirror of the audience.

title: Rosas danst Rosas
note: Four women, some chairs, and a relentless rhythm of sighs, hair flicks and collapses. De Keersmaeker's breakthrough piece fuses minimalist rigour with fierce, everyday femininity, and it still looks startlingly fresh.

title: In the Middle, Somewhat Elevated
note: Ballet pushed to its extreme: limbs flung past the point of balance, to Thom Willems' crashing electronic score. Forsythe's 1987 work blew open classical technique, and this pas de deux shows its cool ferocity at full tilt.

title: The Time of Your Life
note: Gecko's piece sweeps through a single life in vivid, physical images. Amit Lahav's company blends dance, theatre and multilingual voices into something both dreamlike and deeply human. This is the full show.

title: Il n'est pas encore minuit...
note: A crowd of acrobats builds towers of bodies, hurls each other skyward and catches every fall with total trust. Compagnie XY makes circus a collective act, and the joy of the group is as thrilling as the danger.

title: Music for 18 Musicians
artist: Steve Reich / eighth blackbird & Third Coast Percussion
note: A full live performance of Reich's shimmering masterpiece by eighth blackbird, the score that so many choreographers have danced to. Pulsing marimbas, voices and clarinets breathe in waves, and watching the musicians pass patterns between them is its own kind of choreography.

title: JOHN
note: Built from real interviews, JOHN tells one man's life story of crime, addiction and survival through speech and restless movement. DV8's verbatim physical theatre is raw and unflinching, and the bodies say what words can't.
